genes/PSEAE/cdhA/cdhA-ai-review.yaml.description: cdhA (PA5386) encodes the cytoplasmic NAD(+)-dependent L-carnitine dehydrogenase of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The enzyme oxidizes L-carnitine to 3-dehydrocarnitine, the first committed step of the aerobic route by which P. aeruginosa uses L-carnitine as a sole carbon and nitrogen source; CdhC then cleaves 3-dehydrocarnitine with acetyl-CoA to betainyl-CoA and acetoacetate, and CdhB hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA to glycine betaine. The purified enzyme is specific for L-carnitine and NAD(+), and the gene is part of the carnitine-induced PA5388-PA5384 locus required for growth on carnitine.

review.summary: CdhA is a soluble cytoplasmic enzyme.
review.reason: The HAMAP rule for L-carnitine dehydrogenases places the enzyme in the cytoplasm, and the protein has no signal peptide or transmembrane segment; its substrates L-carnitine and NAD(+) are intracellular after uptake.

supported_by.supporting_text: SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Cytoplasm {ECO:0000255|HAMAP-Rule:MF_02129}.

review.summary: InterPro2GO transfer from the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase domains; CdhA oxidizes free L-carnitine, not a fatty acid or acyl-CoA.
review.reason: The mapping is correct for the acyl-CoA dehydrogenases of the domain family but wrong for the L-carnitine dehydrogenase subfamily. The purified enzyme does not act on 3-hydroxybutyrate or other hydroxy acids, and its physiological role is carnitine catabolism.

supported_by.supporting_text: D,L-3- hydroxybutyrate, L-lactate, ethanol, L-malate and D,L-isocitrate are not substrates (PubMed:4302217).
Belongs to the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase family. L- carnitine dehydrogenase subfamily.

source_defects.explanation: InterPro2GO maps IPR006108/IPR006176/IPR022694 (3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase domains) to fatty acid metabolic process. The L-carnitine dehydrogenase subfamily (IPR026578, HAMAP MF_02129) shares these domains but does not act on fatty acids; the InterPro mapping should exclude it.

genes/PSEAE/cdhB/cdhB-ai-review.yaml.description: cdhB (PA5385) encodes the betainyl-CoA thioesterase of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a hotdog-fold acyl-CoA thioesterase (PANTHER PTHR31793 subfamily SF2) that hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA (N,N,N-trimethylglycyl-CoA) to glycine betaine and free coenzyme A. This is the last step of aerobic L-carnitine catabolism after CdhA and CdhC, and it regenerates the CoA consumed by CdhC. Despite the legacy name "betainyl-CoA thiolase", the protein is a hydrolase, not a thiolase. cdhB is induced by carnitine through CdhR and is required for growth on carnitine.

genes/PSEAE/Q9HTH6/Q9HTH6-ai-review.yaml.description: PA5388 encodes CaiX, the periplasmic L-carnitine-binding protein of the Cbc (choline/betaine/carnitine) ABC importer of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. CaiX has a cleavable signal peptide and an OpuAC-type substrate-binding domain; it binds carnitine with moderate affinity, docks to the shared CbcWV permease-ATPase core, and confers carnitine specificity on it. CaiX is required for carnitine uptake and for growth on carnitine, and with CbcWV it is sufficient for carnitine but not choline or glycine betaine uptake.

review.summary: The uptake assays show carnitine transport, but carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound, and GO does not place carnitine transport under amine transport.
review.reason: The experiment supports the carnitine-specific term already on this protein (GO:0015226). An OLS4 query of the GO hierarchy (PSEPK/cbcW/cbcW-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md, hierarchicalAncestors, run 2026-11-04) shows GO:0015226, GO:0015879 and GO:1902603 sit under quaternary ammonium group transport (GO:0015697/GO:0015651) and not under GO:0005275 or GO:0015837. The amine term is therefore a lateral mis-placement of the substrate class, not a true-but-broad ancestor, and is replaced rather than kept as non-core. The genes/human/SLC22A5 review keeps GO:0015837 on a carnitine transporter as correct but general; the difference from that precedent is deliberate and follows the OLS placement.

supported_by.supporting_text: As expected, MKH13 cells coexpressing cbcWV (on pNcbcWV) and caiX (on a pTOK2T derivative) were able to take up carnitine but not choline and betaine, demonstrating that CaiX was sufficient for, and specific to, carnitine uptake (Table 5).

The row is kept and the qualifier error recorded as a source defect, the convention used for the CbcW and CbcV rows and for the BenB subunit in genes/ACIAD/benB; the core function records CaiX with contributes_to, because translocation requires the CbcW permease and CbcV ATPase.
